source: Hyun Hee Hong, Mina K. Kim (2020). "Comparison of orthonasal thresholds of key volatile flavor compounds responsible for traditional doenjang flavor in two matrices: Water-based and soybean-based model system". Journal of Sensory Studies 2020;e12567 (article number; no volume/page). DOI 10.1111/joss.12567. Short Contribution, 5 pages. Fermented Food Research Center, Jeonbuk (Chonbuk) National University, Jeonju-si, South Korea. NRF-2017R1D1A3B03032520.
units: ug/kg (micrograms per kilogram) as printed for BOTH matrices. Basis caveat: the soybean matrix is dosed by mass (12 g), so ug/kg is dimensionally correct there; the water matrix is dosed by volume (12 mL), so ug/kg is being used for what is really ug/L. At water density the two coincide to <0.5%. Ratios are dimensionless (soybean BET / water BET).
method: Orthonasal best-estimate thresholds (BET) by 7-series 3-Ascending Forced Choice (7-3AFC), ASTM E679-91 (ASTM 1997), factor-3 ascending dilution series (7 steps => 729x span nominal). Panel n = 20, recruited by campus flyers and word of mouth among departmental friends, staff and faculty; instructed on proper sniffing technique; NO screening or performance criterion reported; number of replicate sessions per panellist NOT stated. 1 min rest between each set of three; panellists instructed to sniff their sleeves between cups (per Leksrisompong et al. 2010). Cups: 70 mL (70 mm x 30 mm) white opaque lidded plastic, three-digit random codes. Blanks were matrix-matched (same 12 mL water / 12 g soybean). Individual BET rule: geometric mean of the last concentration with an incorrect answer and the first with a correct answer; a 'not sure' on a correct choice multiplied that concentration by 1.41 before the geometric mean (per Lawless, Hartono & Hernandez 2000). Group BET = geometric mean of the individual BETs. Serving temperature not stated (room temperature implied). MATRIX A (water) = distilled water, 12 mL per cup, aliquot of 70% ethanol stock spiked in and served immediately -- NO equilibration hold. MATRIX B (soybean) = 2.5 kg soybeans (local grocery, Jeonju) soaked in 3 L distilled water 20 h at room temperature, autoclaved 40 min at 121 C / 0.1 MPa, cooled, ground in a food processor 1 min at 24000 rpm; 12 g per cup; spiked one compound at a time, bagged in polyethylene, stomached 30 s at 8 strokes/s, vacuum-sealed, stored 4 C for 24 h. Soybean model basis cited to Park, Hwang, Jung & Lee (2002), 'standard method of manufacturing soybean paste'. Compound selection basis cited to Jo, Cho, Song, Shin & Kim (2011). All compounds from Sigma-Aldrich (St. Louis, MO); purities not stated; stock solvent 70% ethanol, vortex-homogenised. Soybean matrix pH, protein, fat and moisture are ALL unstated. Same panel, same day, same protocol and same BET rule for both matrices => the paired ratios are same_study_same_method (cross_study_cross_method: FALSE).

provenance_fields.equilibration_asymmetric: true (water 0 h @ ~22 C vs soybean 24 h @ 4 C)
provenance_fields.anchor: Table 2, p. 3 (BET values); Table 1, p. 2 (dosing series)

compounds.name: 2,3-dimethyl pyrazine
compounds.class: alkylpyrazine (1,4-diazine heteroaromatic); aroma description as printed: 'Nutty-roast' [Akiyama et al. 2005]
compounds.notes: Printed dispersion +/- 0.6 (soy) and 0.7 (water), scale not stated (assumed log10 decades). Dlog10 = +1.689. Printed Z column value 19173 -- DO NOT INGEST (it is BET2-BET1, not a test statistic). log P as cited by the paper: 0.54. Table 1 caveat: the soybean dosing range 1800-145800 ug/kg spans only 81x = 3^4, i.e. a FIVE-step series, inconsistent with the stated 7-step design. On the SD convention the paper says it used, this compound's shift computes to |Z| = 1.83, below 1.96. The paper's mechanistic sentence about this compound ('two methyl groups and amino group', 'methyl group increases the water-solubility') is chemically wrong on both halves -- pyrazine has no amino group and methyl substitution decreases water solubility; the number is unaffected but the reasoning must not be propagated.

compounds.name: Ethyl-4-methylpentanoate
compounds.class: branched-chain aliphatic ester; aroma description as printed: 'Citrus, pineapple' [Kishimoto, Wanikama, Kono & Shibata 2006]
compounds.notes: The single inverted compound in the set; no other paper in the corpus reports an inversion. Printed dispersion +/- 0.9 (water), 0.5 (soy), scale not stated. Dlog10 = -0.811. Printed Z column value -8.1 -- DO NOT INGEST. log P as cited: 2.10. LOAD-BEARING CAVEAT: the paper's claim '(p < .05)' for this compound is unsupported -- no p-value is computed anywhere in the paper, and on the SD convention the paper explicitly says it used, the correct Z is -0.79 (NOT significant); it reaches significance (-3.52) only on the SE = SD/sqrt(20) delta-method convention the paper says it departed from. The inversion is real in the point estimates but its significance is convention-dependent.

compounds.name: 2-pentyl furan
compounds.class: alkylfuran (oxygen heteroaromatic); aroma description as printed: 'Licorice, beany' [Lam & Proctor 2003]
compounds.notes: Printed dispersion +/- 0.7 (water), 0.6 (soy), scale not stated. Dlog10 = +3.133. Printed Z column value 11681 -- DO NOT INGEST. log P as cited: 3.70 (the most hydrophobic compound in the set). One of the two canonical beany markers that autoclaved ground soybean is itself rich in -- relevant to the paper's background-masking proposal (no background concentrations were measured).

compounds.name: Hexanal
compounds.class: straight-chain saturated aliphatic aldehyde (C6); aroma description as printed: 'Green/sweet' [Carunchia-Whetstine, Cadwallader & Drake 2005]
compounds.notes: Printed dispersion +/- 0.8 (water), 0.7 (soy), scale not stated. Dlog10 = +2.122. Printed Z column value 1657 -- DO NOT INGEST. log P as cited: 1.77. Dossier calls this the only defensible hexanal matrix factor in the corpus (same panel, same method); it sits ~1 order of magnitude above the Vega 1994 3% gelatin cross-study figure and ~1 order below the Brewer 1995 cooked-beef figure, and is cited as independent corroboration of the proposed Brewer reclassification to dose_added_pre_cook. Cannot be rescaled to another protein loading because the soybean matrix composition is not reported.

compounds.name: 3-methyl butanal
compounds.class: branched saturated aliphatic aldehyde (C5, Strecker aldehyde of leucine); aroma description as printed: 'Dark chocolate/malty' [Carunchia-Whetstine, Cadwallader & Drake 2005]
compounds.notes: Printed dispersion +/- 0.6 in both matrices, scale not stated. Dlog10 = +2.420. Printed Z column value 131 -- DO NOT INGEST. log P as cited: 1.79. This row is the clearest proof that the +/- column cannot be a linear SD: a linear reading gives 120% RSD on the water BET of 0.5 against +/- 0.6. Two cited prior aqueous values for this compound differ from each other by 800x (0.2 vs 160 ug/kg).

Table 1 caveat: the soybean dosing range is printed as 400-29160 ug/kg = 72.9x, and 400 is the only value in the whole of Table 1 that is not an exact member of its own geometric series (360 x 3^4 = 29160 exactly); the dossier's most parsimonious reading is a typo for 360, explicitly not asserted.

aggregate_statistics_derived_by_dossier.note: All aggregate statistics are class [Z] -- derived by the extraction wave, never printed by the authors.

notes: CAVEATS PRINTED IN THE DOSSIER. (1) CAS numbers are NOT printed anywhere in the paper or the dossier; all cas fields are null. Chemical 'class' strings are NOT printed by the authors either -- they are assigned here from the compound names; only the aroma descriptions quoted inside each class string are as printed (with their cited sources). (2) The +/- column's scale is NEVER stated and cannot be linear -- a linear reading implies 0.0024% RSD on 4-vinyl phenol/soybean and 120% on 3-methyl butanal/water. The only self-consistent reading is SDs of the log-transformed individual BETs (0.4-0.9, mean 0.65 decades), but the base of the logarithm is not stated; the dossier assumes log10 and records dispersion_scale: log10_assumed_not_stated. Uncertainty use is a hard blocker until the base is confirmed. (3) The printed Z column is NOT the formula the paper writes down: every printed Z equals the raw difference BET2 - BET1 in ug/kg to within 1.4%, so the denominator was effectively 1.00 rather than sqrt(SD1^2 + SD2^2). Do not ingest the Z column and do not use it to decide significance. (4) Asymmetric equilibration: the water arm was served immediately at ~22 C (0 h hold) while the soybean arm was vacuum-sealed and held 24 h at 4 C. This is a protocol asymmetry, not a matrix property, and it is confounded with every paired ratio in this file. (5) The soybean matrix composition is entirely unreported -- not pH, not protein, not fat, not moisture, not solids -- so no ratio here can be rescaled to another protein or lipid loading, nor decomposed into protein and lipid terms. matrix_composition: not_stated is mandatory on all ten records. (6) Three Table 1 dosing ranges are inconsistent with the stated 7-step series (butyric acid/water 81x; 2,3-dimethylpyrazine/soybean 81x; dimethyl disulfide/soybean 72.9x). All 20 group BETs nonetheless fall inside their own printed series ranges, checked cell by cell, so no BET is an extrapolation beyond its series. (7) Number of replicate sessions per panellist is never stated. (8) Panel was untrained-but-instructed, Korean population, single institution, 2019 -- population-specific. (9) The paper mis-cites Guadagni, Buttery & Turnbaugh (1972) to Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry; the correct venue is Journal of the Science of Food and Agriculture 23, 1435-1444 (right volume/pages). It also cites 'Karagul-Yuceer et al. (2003)' in text against a 2004 reference-list entry; not resolvable from the PDF. (10) The paper's own aqueous arm disagrees with cited prior aqueous values by up to 1,416x, and two cited prior water values for the same compound (butyric acid) differ from each other by 5,540x -- cross-study aqueous orthonasal reproducibility is worse than three orders of magnitude, which is precisely why the WITHIN-study ratios in this file are the load-bearing quantity. (11) Mechanism note from the dossier: hydrophobicity does not predict the shift (r = -0.052 over the ten compounds) and the sign of the null slope is opposite to what binding or partition predicts, which the dossier treats as the strongest single-study refutation of a partition/binding account in the corpus; the authors' own proposal, background-odour masking, is recorded as a named candidate mechanism but is NOT proven -- no background concentrations were measured. (12) Declaration Amendment 4 (2026-08-28) assigns these ten paired ratios GATING HOLD-OUT status. This file is frozen evidence: it must never be read by, or fed into, any model-building or fitting wave.
